evidence.field: 字形演變；字形來源說明
evidence.text: The entry lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen materials for 牛. Its explanation says the graph emphasizes the ox’s head and horns and originally referred to the animal. The sequence is a record of graphic forms; the page does not provide dates for each listed specimen in the inspected text.
evidence.title: 漢字「牛」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi entry and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry transmits Xu Shen’s account: “大牲也” and describes the graph as depicting horns, head, and a raised back/tail feature. Duan Yucai disputes the transmitted gloss and proposes “事也。理也,” explaining 牛 through its work and the dissectible patterns of the animal. This is a historical lexicographic interpretation and later commentary, not independent confirmation of the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「牛」

evidence.source: Unicode Consortium, Unicode Standard, CJK Radicals Supplement names list
evidence.text: Unicode identifies ⺧ as a variant of Kangxi radical 93 and points to 牛 U+725B; this concerns the radical form and does not establish the ancient graphic history of 牛.
evidence.title: CJK Radicals Supplement

evidence.source: Local Unihan reading row; upstream character-specific page could not be inspected
evidence.text: The supplied exact local row gives current Mandarin niú. The official character-specific Unihan page was attempted but inaccessible through the web tool, so this local reading is not presented as externally verified click-through evidence.
evidence.title: Unihan record for U+725B (attempted; inaccessible)

search_audit.outcome: Inspected Academia Sinica character evolution entry and Shuowen entry/commentary. Search returned Unicode radical references, but did not verify the requested character-specific kMandarin row; direct page remained inaccessible.

gaps: The paleographic database lists inscriptional periods and corpus references but the inspected page text does not date individual 牛 attestations or state the earliest securely dated specimen.

No specific early textual attestations were inspected to establish when the written graph was used for the animal sense or to document later semantic extensions. The dossier’s modern gloss list does not establish chronology.
No sound component is proposed for 牛. Current readings and historical reconstructions therefore do not provide evidence of phonetic composition.
The supplied local kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows were checked as provided, but the official character-specific Unihan page could not be verified externally in this session.

No evidence of graphic corruption or a competing formation analysis beyond the received Shuowen account and the Academia Sinica database’s pictographic interpretation was found in the inspected pages.
